The biggest challenge of building large projects is figuring out what the customer actually needs, formalizing that in precise language and properly communicating it.
That is what the picture is trying to convey.
And that is exactly the opposite of what AI is good at.
AI will make these issues worse, ship more of what people ask for and less of what they actually need.
I guess you could say AI does at least help you fail faster and find issues in the requirements earlier.

You're touching something real: AI is great at executing what you describe, terrible at questioning whether you described useful thing.
AI isn't designed to define what to deliver. That's on us.
What if we close that loop? People Ask → AI Ships → measure actual usage, maybe surveys too (though people tend to lie in those 😅) → AI suggests adjustments based on real data.
Make the "fail faster" part of the system, not just a side effect. The cycle becomes: ship → observe → rewrite requirements → regenerate.
Still not perfect and not ready now. But when iteration is cheap, you can afford to be wrong faster — and fix it faster too.
